notes:
Summary: Lighthouse Inference Labs evaluating Redwood Dedicated for low-latency, high-throughput conversational and reranking workloads. Primary objective is deterministic latency under reserved capacity + clear measurement alignment between Redwood and Lighthouse tooling.

Customer quotes / shorthand: "We need guarantees you can measure from our client path — not just infra-side numbers. p95 visible to product users must be <150ms for single-turn chat."

Latency SLO alignment (discussion points):
- Definitions: p50/p95/p99 = client-visible end-to-end latency percentiles measured at the SDK edge unless otherwise noted. Agree to capture both client-side first-byte and server-complete timings.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: streaming SLOs target time-to-first-token (TTFT) and time-per-token steady-state. Non-streaming SLOs measure total response latency (request -> last byte). Separate SLAs required.
- Measurement boundaries: Customer wants TLS handshake, DNS, and SDK processing included for client-side; Redwood suggests providing both server-only and client-visible views. Action: agree on mapping and a reconciliation run.
- Warm vs cold KV-cache: benchmark windows will include cold-warm mix representative of production traces (approx 70% warm, 30% cold). Ensure SLOs call out expected warm-cache distribution.
- Percentile goals (proposal): non-streaming p50 <= 30ms (server), p95 <= 120ms (server), p99 <= 320ms (server). Client-visible targets: p50 <= 60ms, p95 <= 150ms, p99 <= 400ms. Streaming: TTFT p50 <= 15ms server, p95 <= 60ms. These are starting points for negotiation.

Throughput / reserved GPU planning notes:
- Workload: average request size 24 tokens, 99th token spike to 512 tokens for long-form reranking tasks.
- Target steady-state QPS: 450 requests/sec (mixed chat+rerank). Peak bursts up to 900 QPS for 10-30s windows.
- Initial Redwood recommendation: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved with autoscale headroom to handle burst windows; quantify via 48h stress test.
- Batching policy: continuous batching with max latency budgets per route; customer requests explicit control to cap batch waits at 8ms for chat route.

SLA negotiation items:
- Remedies: credit model for p95 misses vs uptime SLA. Customer prefers monetary credit and ability to trigger canary rollback automatically.
- Measurement authority: propose joint run (Redwood-run harness + Lighthouse SDK agent) and shared artifacts (logs, pcap-lite traces) for 48h baseline.

Action items & success criteria:
- Redwood to provide a measurement script (k6 + SDK wrapper) that reproduces client-side instrumentation by 2026-03-12 (DEMO).
- Run 48h dedicated capacity stress test (scheduled 2026-03-17 to 2026-03-19). Deliverables: percentile reports (client and server), sample traces, GPU utilization, batch size histogram.
- If p95 client-visible <= 150ms sustained at target QPS and burst policy holds for 95% of bursts, move to procurement and reserved contract.

Open questions / risks:
- Exact definition of streaming p95 across multi-token responses (do we evaluate TTFT only or aggregate per-response tail?). Need alignment.
- Legal: data residency clause language and encryption-at-rest proof required before procurement.
- Cost sensitivity: they want a modeled ARR and token cost estimate tied to a production trace sample.
